Clause: «تابوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين). Clause: «أصلحوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause.
Clause: «إنّ الله غفور ... » has no grammatical position, being a justification for something implied, i.e. "He forgave them".
6- (الواو) is conjunctive. (الذين) like the first. The second (الواو) is circumstantial. (لهم) attached to the predicate of يكن. (إلّا) is for exception. (أنفسهم) a substitute for شهداء, nominative [Note: Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted making it an adjective of شهداء, with (إلّا) in the sense of غير, by analogy with His saying, the Exalted: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلّا الله.], (الفاء) is redundant. (شهادة) a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is (أربع). (بالله) attached to (شهادات) [Note: it is not permissible to attach it to شهادة, lest the maṣdar be separated from its object by an outsider, namely the predicate.], and the (اللام) in (لمن) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis.
Clause: «الذين يرمون ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause الذين يرمون (the first).
Clause: «يرمون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «لم يكن لهم شهداء» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the pronoun in (لهم).
Clause: «شهادة أحدهم أربع ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (الذين); the fāʾ was added to the predicate because the relative resembles a condition.
Clause: «إنّه لمن الصادقين» is in the position of an accusative, governed by the maṣdar شهادات. The hamza of (إنّ) ought to have had fatḥa, but the lām in the predicate made it kasra, so the maṣdar was suspended (ʿulliqa) from direct operation.
7- (الخامسة) a mubtadaʾ, nominative. (عليه) attached to the predicate of أنّ. (كان) a defective past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis. (من الكاذبين) attached to the predicate of كان.. and the noun of كان is a latent pronoun referring to أحدهم.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لعنة الله عليه) is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (الخامسة).
Clause: «الخامسة أنّ لعنة الله..» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause شهادة أحدهم.
Clause: «كان من الكاذبين» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.. The apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "if he is among the liars, then the curse is upon him".
8- (الواو) is conjunctive. (عنها) attached to (يدرأ). (أربع) an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, being its number. (بالله) attached to (تشهد). (إنّه لمن الكاذبين) like إنّه لمن الصادقين.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تشهد أربع ... ) is in the position of a nominative, agent of يدرأ.
Clause: «يدرأ ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause فشهادة ... [Note: or resumptive, having no position.].
Clause: «تشهد ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «إنّه لمن الكاذبين» is in the position of an accusative, governed by the maṣdar شهادات ...
9- (الواو) is conjunctive. (الخامسة) conjoined to أربع, accusative [Note: or a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being تشهد, in which case the wāw conjoins clauses.]. (عليها) attached to the predicate of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ غضب الله عليها) is in the position of an accusative, a substitute for الخامسة [Note: it is possible that it be genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. "that the wrath of Allah..", attached to the implied verb تشهد.].
(إن كان من الصادقين) is like إن كان من الكاذبين. Clause: «إن كان من الصادقين» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "then the wrath is upon her".
10- (الواو) is conjunctive. (لولا) is a non-jussive conditional particle - a particle denoting impossibility due to existence. (فضل) a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is necessarily omitted, its implied form being «موجود». (عليكم) attached to (فضل). (حكيم) a second predicate of أنّ, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله توّاب ... ) is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the explicit maṣdar فضل.
Clause: «لولا فضل الله ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause الذين يرمون. The apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being «لهلكتم» ("you would have perished"), or «لبيّن الحقّ» ("the truth would have been made clear").. etc., according to the accepted interpretation.

* Morphology:
(4) يرمون: it contains an alteration by omission. Its origin is يرميون; the ḍamma was found heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made sukūn and its vowel was transferred to the mīm before it, then the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns: the sukūn of the final radical of the word and the sukūn of the plural pronoun. So it became يرمون, its pattern يفعون.
(7) (الخامسة): a name of the number on the pattern فاعل, since it indicates order; it came in the feminine because it is an adjective of a feminine, namely الشهادة.

* Rhetoric:
Metaphor (istiʿāra):
In His saying, the Exalted, «وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَناتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا» etc., "throwing" is borrowed for reviling with the indecency of adultery, since it is an offence by speech; and reviling with this indecency is called qadhf (slanderous accusation).
Iltifāt (shift of address):
In His saying, the Exalted, «وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ» there is an iltifāt toward the accusers and the accused women, by way of preponderance (taghlīb), to give the occasion of gracious favour its due; and the apodosis of «لولا» is omitted to make it awesome, as if there were no expression that could encompass its explanation, and this is common in their speech.

* Benefits:
1- Among the penalties (ḥudūd) in Islam:
The penalty for the adulterer or adulteress, whether married (muḥṣan) or not, is well known in Islam, and its aim is to protect the family on the one hand and the soundness of lineages on the other.
But what is worth mentioning and drawing attention to is the penalty for those who accuse chaste women and charge honourable women with indecency without having sufficient proof, which is a doubled testimony compared with the testimonies for other rights. For all other rights the proof of two witnesses suffices, but whoever slanders honourable women and charges them with indecency commits a grave matter in the Law and a great transgression against the rights of others; for this accusation may result in the destruction of a family, the dispersal of children, and misery for the spouses. This fabrication may even lead to crime. Therefore proof of it is established only by four witnesses. Allah has condemned the one who commits this sin and threatened him with material punishment, namely that he be flogged eighty lashes before a gathering of people, and with moral punishment that strips him of probity, so that no testimony of his is accepted; then He, glory be to Him, branded them with depravity and departure from the principles of the religion.
How often we see in the circles of our society those who find it easy to slander chaste, honourable women and take it as a pretext for taking revenge on the husband or the wife, or on the whole family.
It is regrettable that the likes of these slip out of the bond of the law, and no punishment reaches them.
2- Categories of spouses:
a- The adulterer desires only an adulteress.
b- The adulteress desires only an adulterer.
c- The chaste man desires only a chaste woman.
d- The chaste woman desires only a chaste man.
He, glory be to Him, the Exalted, mentioned the first two categories and was silent about the other two, because they are inferred from the flow of the speech, so there is no need to mention them. The Qur'an always and forever inclines to brevity because it is a kind of inimitability (iʿjāz).
3- Mutual cursing (mulāʿana).
This verse contains a special ruling in a case in which there is no witness at all. The husband, who is one of the two parties, may see on his wife something that stains his honour and accuse her of adultery without having a witness to it; so he calls Allah to witness four times that he is truthful, and as for the fifth, he accepts the curse upon himself if he is lying in his claim.
The result of that is that she deserves to have the penalty carried out on her, unless she calls Allah to witness four times that her husband is lying, and then invokes that Allah's wrath be upon her if her husband is truthful in his claim.. This formula, which the jurists have called «mulāʿana», is an exceptional and exemplary procedure for an incident that occurs with no proof except conscience and trust.
4- The apodosis of «لولا» may be omitted for magnification, as in the verse «وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ حَكِيمٌ».

safi-cedvel:11-13.t:
* I'rab:
(بالإفك) attached to (جاؤوا). (عصبة) predicate of (إنّ), nominative. (منكم) attached to an adjective of (عصبة). (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive lā. (شرا) the second direct object. (لكم) attached to an adjective of (شرّا). (بل) is for the transitional iḍrāb (turning away). The second (لكم) is attached to an adjective of (خير). (لكلّ) attached to an omitted predicate placed first. (منهم) attached to an adjective of (امرئ). (ما) is a maṣdar particle. (من الإثم) attached to (اكتسب).. The interpreted maṣdar (ما اكتسب ... )
is in the position of a nominative, a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(الواو) is conjunctive. (الذي) a relative noun, mubtadaʾ, whose predicate is the clause له عذاب.. (منهم) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of تولّى. (له) attached to a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ (عذاب)..
Clause: «إنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «جاؤوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «لا تحسبوه ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «هو خير لكم ... » has no grammatical position, being a resumption that emphasizes what precedes.
Clause: «لكلّ امرئ.. ما اكتسب» has no grammatical position, being another explanatory resumption.
Clause: «اكتسب ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما) [Note: it is permissible that (ما) be a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense of what he earned"..
and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «اكتسبه», and the preposition and its genitive after it are attached to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun.].
Clause: «الذي تولّى ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause لكلّ امرئ..
Clause: «تولّى كبره ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
Clause: «له عذاب ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (الذي).
12- (لولا) is a particle of reproach and urging. (إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable, attached to (ظنّ). The (الواو) in (سمعتموه) is redundant, a lengthening of the vowel of the mīm. (بأنفسهم) attached to the second direct object. (الواو) is conjunctive. (مبين) an adjective of إفك, nominative like it.
Clause: «سمعتموه ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «ظنّ المؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ظنّ.
Clause: «هذا إفك ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
13- (لولا) is a particle of reproach and regret. (عليه) attached to (جاؤوا), by implying in it the meaning of "they brought witnesses". (بأربعة) attached to (جاؤوا). (شهداء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa. (الفاء) is conjunctive. (إذ) an adverb of past time, containing the meaning of condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «كذبوا» ("they lied"), which the content of the verse explains in His saying: أولئك هم الكاذبون. (بالشهداء) attached to (يأتوا). (الفاء) is redundant, linking the apodosis to the condition [Note: similar to this is His saying, the Exalted: (وَإِذْ لَمْ يَهْتَدُوا بِهِ فَسَيَقُولُونَ هذا إِفْكٌ..) «al-Aḥqāf, verse 11».]. (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to (الكاذبون). (هم) a pronoun of separation [Note: or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is الكاذبون, the clause being the predicate of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.].
Clause: «جاؤوا ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «لم يأتوا ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «أولئك.. الكاذبون» has no position, being in the status of the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

* Morphology:
(الإفك): a noun meaning lying, or the worst of it; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.
(امرئ): a noun meaning "human being"; the rāʾ takes the vowel of the final letter: you say جاء امرؤ, رأيت امرأ, مررت بامرئ. Its feminine is امرأة, and the (hamza) is a hamzat waṣl; the definite article (أل) enters it only rarely, as in المرأة.
(كبره): a noun meaning the greater part of the matter, from the triliteral verb كبر, bāb فرح; its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Expressing others by "selves":
In His saying, the Exalted, «ظَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتُ بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ خَيْراً» this expression contains the most far-reaching of subtle points and the richest in lofty meanings. The secret of this expression is to incline the believer toward his brother and reproach him for mentioning him with evil, picturing that as the image of one who proceeds to slander himself and accuse himself of an indecency that is not in him, and nothing is more hideous than that.
2- Iltifāt:
In His saying, the Exalted, «ظَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتُ» the flow of the speech would be to say «لولا إذ سمعتموه ظننتم بأنفسكم خيرا وقلتم», but He turned from the second person to the third, and from the pronoun to the overt noun, to be emphatic in the reproach by way of iltifāt, and to state the word "faith" explicitly, as an indication that partnership in it requires that no believing man accept against his brother, nor believing woman against her sister, the word of an absent speaker or a defamer.

* Benefits:
1- The hadith of the slander (ḥadīth al-ifk).
It is reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim that ʿĀʾisha said: I was with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) on a campaign, after the veil had been revealed. When he had finished with it he returned, and drew near Medina, and he gave permission one night for departure. I walked and relieved myself, then came back to the camel litter, and behold, my necklace had broken, so I went back looking for it. They lifted my howdah, thinking I was in it, for the women were light, eating only a morsel of food. I found my necklace, and came after they had gone, so I sat in the place where I had been, thinking that the people would miss me and return to me. Then my eyes overcame me and I slept. Ṣafwān had camped for the night behind the army, so he set out late in the night for rest, and saw the dark form of a sleeping person. He recognized me when he saw me, for he used to see me before the veil. I woke at his saying "Innā lillāh" when he recognized me, and I covered my face. By Allah, he did not speak a word to me and I heard no word from him except his saying "Innā lillāh" when he made his mount kneel. Then he went off leading the mount with me until we reached the army after they had halted, in the heat of the noon. So whoever perished concerning me perished, and the one who took the greater part of it upon himself among them was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl.
I was ill for a month after we came to Medina, while the people were spreading the words of the people of the slander, and I was aware of none of it. What made me doubtful in my illness was that I did not find from the Messenger of Allah the gentleness I used to see from him when I was ill; the Messenger of Allah would only enter, greet, and then say: "How is that one?"
That made me doubtful, but I was not aware of the evil until I went out after I had convalesced, and Umm Misṭaḥ went out with me toward al-Manāṣiʿ; then we returned, and Umm Misṭaḥ tripped over her wrap, and said: "May Misṭaḥ perish."
I said: "What an evil thing you have said! Do you revile a man who was present at Badr?" She said: "O you naïve one, did you not hear what he said?"
I said: "And what did he say?" She told me the words of the people of the slander, and my illness was increased by it. When I returned to my house I asked permission to go to my parents, wishing to verify the news from them, and he permitted me.
My mother said: "Take it easy, for seldom has a beautiful woman been with a man who loves her, and has co-wives, but they made much of it against her." I said: "Glory be to Allah! And have the people talked about this?" I wept that night until morning, my tears not ceasing and I not sleeping. The Messenger of Allah called ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Usāma ibn Zayd to consult them about parting with his wife. As for Usāma ibn Zayd, he advised the Messenger of Allah according to what he knew of his wife's innocence and of the affection he knew in himself for them, and said to the Messenger of Allah: "They are your family and we know nothing but good."
As for ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: "Allah has not constrained you, and women other than her are many; and if you ask the maidservant she will tell you the truth." So the Messenger of Allah called Barīra to ask her: "Have you seen anything that makes you doubt about ʿĀʾisha?" She said: "No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I have seen nothing in her that I could fault more than that she is a young girl who sleeps over her family's dough, and the domestic animal comes and eats it."
I wept that day of mine, my tears not ceasing and I not sleeping. Then I wept my next night, my tears not ceasing and I not sleeping, and my parents thought that weeping would split my liver. While we were thus, the Messenger of Allah entered, greeted, sat down and recited the testimony, then said: "To proceed: O ʿĀʾisha, such and such has reached me about you. If you are innocent, Allah will soon declare you innocent; and if you have committed a sin, then ask Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses a sin and then repents, Allah turns to him." When the Messenger of Allah finished his speech my tears dried up until I felt not a drop. I said to my father: "Answer the Messenger of Allah for me," and he said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah." I said to my mother: "Answer for me," and she said:
likewise, "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah." I said - and I was a young girl, not reading much of the Qur'an -: "By Allah, I know that you have heard this until it settled in your souls and you believed it. If I say to you that I am innocent, you will not believe me; and if I confess to you something, while Allah knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I find no likeness for me and you except as the father of Yūsuf said: 'So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One sought for help against what you describe.'" Then I turned and lay down on my bed. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah had not left his place, and none of the household had gone out, when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Prophet; and there seized him what used to seize him of the heavy burden at revelation, so that sweat fell from him like pearls on a wintry day. When it was lifted from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), and he was laughing, the first word he spoke was: "Rejoice, O ʿĀʾisha; as for Allah, He has declared you innocent." My mother said to me: "Rise to him." I said: "By Allah I will not rise to him, and I will praise none but Allah, who revealed my innocence".. Abū Bakr used to spend on Misṭaḥ, but stopped that, then the Qur'an was revealed urging him to spend, so Abū Bakr returned to what he had been doing.
2- The tolerance and pardon of Islam:
Abū Bakr swore that he would never again spend on Misṭaḥ after today, since he had walked with the talk of the slander and spread the indecency about the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), and had not regarded Abū Bakr's favour toward him and had not guarded his tongue from error and calumny as Islam commands. What then was the stance of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) and of Abū Bakr toward this weak man who had no one to protect him, had the Messenger wished to seize him, in recompense for the falsehood and calumny his tongue committed?..
You may imagine, dear reader, whatever you wish of recompense and punishment. It may not occur to you that the Messenger of Allah pardoned him, that Allah from His heaven enjoined forgiveness and pardon, and that Abū Bakr went back on his oath, returned to spending on him as usual, and did better.
That is the tolerance of Islam and the pardon of the religion. How beautiful is pardon when one has power, and meeting evil with good! 3- Carrying out the penalty:
Those who spoke about the honour of ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Messenger (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), and slandered her with falsehood and calumny were four: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, Ḥassān ibn Thābit, Misṭaḥ, and Ḥamna bint Jaḥsh. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) carried out against them the command of Allah, namely the flogging of slanderers.
4- Ḥassān ibn Thābit declares ʿĀʾisha innocent in his poetry, saying:
حصان رزان ما تزن بريبة ... وتصبح غرثي من لحوم الغوافل
(Chaste and composed, she is not suspected of any doubtful thing, and she wakes up hungry, not having eaten the flesh of heedless women.)

حليلة خير الناس دينا ومنصبا ... نبي الهدى والمكرمات الفواضل
(Wife of the best of people in religion and rank, the Prophet of guidance and of excellent noble deeds.)

عقيلة حي من لؤي بن غالب ... كرام المساعي مجدها غير زائل
(A noble lady of a tribe from Luʾayy ibn Ghālib, of generous endeavours, her glory unfading.)

مهذبة قد طيب الله جنيها ... وطهرها من كل شين وباطل
(Refined; Allah has made her fruit good and purified her from every blemish and falsehood.)

فإن كان ما بلغت عني قلته ... فلا رفعت سوطي إلي أناملي
(If what has reached you from me is something I said, may my fingertips not raise my whip to me.)

وكيف وودي ما حييت ونصرتي ... بآل رسول الله زين المحافل
(How could it be, when my love and my support, as long as I live, are for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings?)

له رتب عال على الله فضلها ... تقاصر عنها سورة المتطاول
(He has lofty ranks whose merit is with Allah, before which the onslaught of the arrogant falls short.)
5- From the secrets of the development of language:
The word «سبحانك»: originally it was to be mentioned upon seeing something wondrous of His creations, glory be to Him, the Exalted; then it developed with frequent use until it came to be used upon anything one marvels at.
So consider the development of language and its understanding.

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(لولا فضل.. رحمته) its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (10) of this sūra.]. (في الدنيا) attached to (برحمة), and the sign of the genitive is the implied kasra on the alif. (اللام) occurs in the apodosis of لولا. (في ما) attached to (مسّكم); (في) is causal, and (ما) is a relative. (فيه) attached to the verb أفضتم. (عذاب) agent of مسّكم.
Clause: «فضل الله.. (موجود)» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «مسّكم ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «أفضتم ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما) [Note: it is permissible that (ما) be a maṣdar particle, the interpreted maṣdar being in the position of a genitive, with (في) remaining in the sense of causality.].
15- (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of an accusative, attached to an implied verb, i.e. "you sinned" or "you committed sin when you received it" [Note: Abū l-Baqāʾ attached it to the verb مسّكم or أفضتم, and al-Maḥallī followed him in that.]. (تلقّونه) an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs has been dropped. (بألسنتكم) attached to (تلقّونه). (بأفواهكم) attached to an omitted ḥāl from ما - an adjective that precedes the qualified noun [Note: i.e. speech confined to the mouths, without understanding or knowledge.]. (ما) a relative noun, direct object, in the position of an accusative [Note: or an indefinite noun meaning "something", in the position of an accusative as direct object, the clause after it being an adjective of it.]. (لكم) attached to the predicate of ليس. (به) attached to a ḥāl from (علم), which is the postponed noun of ليس, nominative. (هيّنا) the second direct object, accusative. (الواو) is the wāw of ḥāl. (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to (عظيم).
Clause: «تلقّونه ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «تقولون ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause تلقّونه.
Clause: «ليس لكم به علم ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
Clause: «تحسبونه ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause تلقّونه. Clause: «هو.. عظيم» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the object of تحسبونه.

* Rhetoric:
Exaggeration (mubālagha):
In His saying, the Exalted, «وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِكُمْ» — and saying is only ever with the mouth, so what is the meaning of mentioning the mouths? The intent is exaggeration; or it is possible that this speech was not an expression of knowledge established in the heart, but always mere speech of the tongue, as in His saying, the Exalted, «يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ ما لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ».

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (لولا إذ.. قلتم) the i'rab of its counterpart has already been given [Note: in verse (12) of this sūra.], and the adverb is attached to (قلتم). (يكون) a complete imperfect verb in the sense of "it is fitting". (لنا) attached to (يكون). (بهذا) attached to (نتكلّم).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نتكلّم..) is in the position of a nominative, agent of يكون.
(سبحانك) an absolute object of an omitted verb, accusative, brought in to express wonder [Note: al-Zamakhsharī cited this; he said in al-Kashshāf: "If you ask what is the meaning of wonder in the word of glorification, I say: the origin of that is that Allah is glorified upon seeing something wondrous of His creations, then it became frequent until it was used for everything one marvels at, without regard to the meaning of exalting Him above defect..." End.]..
Clause: «سمعتموه ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «قلتم ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «ما يكون لنا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «نتكلّم ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «(نسبّح) سبحانك ... » has no grammatical position, being a parenthetical clause of supplication.
Clause: «هذا بهتان ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.. or a justification for what precedes.

* Rhetoric:
Fronting and postponing:
In His saying, the Exalted, «وَلَوْلا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ قُلْتُمْ» the adverb was fronted for an important benefit, namely to make clear that it was obligatory for them, as soon as they heard of the slander, to avoid speaking of it; so, since mention of the time was more important, fronting was necessary.
The secret of wonder:
In His saying, the Exalted, «سُبْحانَكَ». Its meaning is wonder at the greatness of the matter. Its origin is that when a person sees something wondrous of Allah the Exalted's creations he glorifies Him, then it became frequent until it was used at everything one marvels at.

safi-cedvel:17-18.t:
* I'rab:
(لمثله) attached to (تعودوا). (أبدا) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (تعودوا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تعودوا..) is in the position of an accusative, an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "for fear that you return" [Note: it is permissible to imply in (يعظكم) the meaning "forbids you", in which case the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (يعظكم), i.e. "He admonishes you against returning ... that is, He forbids you from returning".].
Clause: «يعظكم الله ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «إن كنتم مؤمنين ... » has no grammatical position, being parenthetical between the two conjoined parts..
The apodosis of the condition is omitted, explained by what precedes, i.e. "so do not return to the like of it"..
18- (الواو) is conjunctive. (لكم) attached to (يبيّن). (الواو) is resumptive. (حكيم) a second predicate, nominative.
Clause: «يبيّن ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يعظكم. Clause: «الله عليم....» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

safi-cedvel:19-20.t:
* I'rab:
(في الذين) attached to (تشيع). (لهم) attached to a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ (عذاب). (في الدنيا) attached to (عذاب). The first (الواو) is resumptive and the second conjunctive. (لا) is negative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تشيع ... ) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object.
Clause: «إنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يحبّون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «تشيع ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «لهم عذاب ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of إنّ.
Clause: «الله يعلم ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يعلم ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
Clause: «أنتم لا تعلمون ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause الله يعلم.
Clause: «لا تعلمون» is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).
20- (الواو) is conjunctive. (لولا فضل.. رحيم) the i'rab of its counterpart, in words and clauses, has already been given «1».

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) an indefinite specified one addressed (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative. (الذين) a relative in the position of an accusative, a substitute for أيّ - or an explicative apposition. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive lā. (الواو) is conjunctive. (من) a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ, in the position of a nominative. (الفاء) links to the apodosis - or is causal. (بالفحشاء) attached to (يأمر). (الواو) is conjunctive. (لولا فضل.. رحمته) its i'rab has already been given «2». (ما) is negative. (منكم) attached to a ḥāl from (أحد), which is genitive in form and nominative in position, the agent of زكى. (أبدا) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (زكى). (الواو) is conjunctive. (من) a relative, direct object. (الواو) is resumptive. (عليم) a second predicate, nominative..
Clause: «النداء وجوابها ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «لا تتّبعوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
Clause: «من يتّبع ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the response to the vocative [Note: or resumptive within the scope of the vocative, or parenthetical between the prohibition and the justification.].
Clause: «يتّبع ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (من).. The apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being «فقد غوى».
Clause: «إنّه يأمر ... » has no grammatical position, being a justification for the prohibition.. or for the condition.
Clause: «يأمر ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of إنّ.
Clause: «لولا فضل الله ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the response to the vocative [Note: it is permissible that it be cut off as a resumption.].
Clause: «ما زكى ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «لكنّ الله ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause لولا فضل الله.
Clause: «يزكّي من يشاء» is in the position of a nominative, predicate of لكنّ.
Clause: «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
Clause: «الله سميع ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal resumption.

* Morphology:
(زكى): it is written in the muṣḥaf with an undotted yāʾ, whereas it should have been written with a long alif, زكا, because its imperfect is يزكو; it contains an alteration (iʿlāl): the weak letter, the lām of the verb, took a vowel after a fatḥa and was changed to alif.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive lā, and the sign of the jussive in (يأتل) is the dropping of the weak letter. (أولو) agent, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw; attached to the masculine plural. (منكم) attached to a ḥāl from the agent. (أولي) direct object, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ. (المساكين) conjoined to أولي by the wāw, accusative, and likewise (المهاجرين). (في سبيل) attached to (المهاجرين).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يؤتوا ... ) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. "in giving" [Note: this is on the view that the meaning of (يأتلي) is "falls short".. But if the meaning is "swears", the implied form is: "that they not give"..
with a negative (لا) implied after the subjunctive أن.].
(الواو) is conjunctive. (اللام) is the lām of command in both places. (ألا) is a particle of offering and urging. (لكم) attached to (يغفر).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يغفر الله ... ) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object.
Clause: «لا يأتل أولو ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يؤتوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the first particle-like relative (أن). Clause: «يعفوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «يصفحوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause or to يعفوا. Clause: «تحبّون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يغفر الله ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «الله غفور ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal resumption.

* Morphology:
(يأتل): it contains an alteration by omission, in keeping with the jussive; its pattern is يفتع.
(أولو): a collective noun with no singular from its own wording, and it has a singular in meaning, namely ذو. In i'rab it is attached to the sound masculine plural, so it is nominative with wāw and accusative and genitive with yāʾ. See verse (197) of Sūrat al-Baqara.

safi-cedvel:23-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الغافلات، المؤمنات) two adjectives of المحصنات, accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; and the (الواو) in (لعنوا) is the deputy agent. (في الدنيا) attached to (لعنوا). (الواو) is conjunctive. (لهم) attached to a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ (عذاب).
Clause: «إنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يرمون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «لعنوا ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of إنّ.
Clause: «لهم عذاب ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لعنوا.
24- (يوم) an adverb, accusative, attached to the "settledness" (istiqrār) to which the predicate is attached [Note: it is not permissible to attach it to عذاب - in the opinion of the Basrans - because it is a maṣdar described before it has operated.]. (عليهم) attached to (تشهد). (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا ... ) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (تشهد).
Clause: «تشهد.. ألسنتهم» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «كانوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما).
Clause: «يعملون» is in the position of an accusative, predicate of كانوا.
25- (يومئذ) attached to (يوفّيهم) [Note: or attached to (يعملون).], and the tanwīn is a substitute for an omitted clause, the implied form being:
"on the day when it testifies against them". (هو) a pronoun of separation [Note: or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is الحقّ, the nominal clause being the predicate of أنّ.]. (الحقّ) predicate of أنّ, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله.. الحقّ) is in the position of an accusative, standing in for the two objects of يعلمون.
Clause: «يوفّيهم ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «يعلمون ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يوفّيهم.

* Morphology:
(الغافلات): plural of الغافلة, feminine of الغافل, an active participle from the triliteral verb غفل; its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
Generality:
In His saying, the Exalted, «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَناتِ».
By المحصنات He intended generality, even though the account was prompted by ʿĀʾisha. The aim of mentioning them in general is the threat to whoever falls upon ʿĀʾisha, in the most emphatic way: for if this is the threat to one who slanders individual believing women, what is to be thought of the threat to one who falls into slandering their lady! Moreover, generalizing the threat is more emphatic and decisive than specifying it, and for this reason Zulaykhā generalized when she said «ما جَزاءُ مَنْ أَرادَ بِأَهْلِكَ سُوءاً إِلَّا أَنْ يُسْجَنَ أَوْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ»; she generalized while intending Yūsuf, to terrify him and alarm him.

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(للخبيثين، للخبيثات، للطيّبين، للطيّبات) each is attached to an omitted predicate of the mubtadaʾ that precedes it. (أولئك) a mubtadaʾ, its predicate is (مبرّؤون), and the indication is to the good men and the good women. (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "what they say of it".].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يقولون) is in the position of a genitive by من, attached to the predicate (مبرّؤون). (لهم) attached to a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ مغفرة.
Clause: «الخبيثات للخبيثين» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «الخبيثون للخبيثات» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «الطيّبات للطيّبين» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «الطيّبون للطيّبات» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «أولئك مبرّؤون ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما).
Clause: «لهم مغفرة ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption [Note: or in the position of a nominative, a second predicate of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).].

* Morphology:
(الخبيثات، الخبيثون): plural of خبيثة and plural of خبيث, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral verb خبث, bāb كرم; its pattern is فعيل. See verse (267) of Sūrat al-Baqara.
(مبرّؤون): plural of مبرّأ, a passive participle from the quadriliteral verb برّأ; its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and a doubled fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:27-28.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها ... بيوتا) like يأيّها.. خطوات [Note: in verse (21) of this sūra.]. (غير) an adjective of (بيوتا), accusative. (حتّى) a particle of limit and of genitive. (تستأنسوا) an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after حتّى. (على أهلها) attached to (تسلّموا)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تستأنسوا ... ) is in the position of a genitive after (حتّى), attached to (تدخلوا).
(لكم) attached to (خير). (تذكّرون) an imperfect verb, nominative, from which one of the two tāʾs has been dropped.
Clause: «يأيّها الذين ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «لا تدخلوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
Clause: «تستأنسوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «تسلّموا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause تستأنسوا.
Clause: «ذلكم خير ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption - or a causal clause. Clause: «لعلّكم تذكّرون» has no grammatical position, being a justification for something implied, i.e. "He revealed this to you so that you may.."
Clause: «تذكّرون» is in the position of a nominative, predicate of لعلّ.
28- (الفاء) is conjunctive. (تجدوا) a jussive imperfect, the protasis [Note: the majority make it jussive by (لم), because that is the stronger in jussive effect, but then the verb no longer indicates the future, since its meaning has turned to the past.. so the i'rab above is better.]. (فيها) attached to (تجدوا). (الفاء) links to the apodosis. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive lā. (حتّى) like the first. (لكم) deputy agent of the passive (يؤذن). The second (لكم) is attached to (قيل). The second (الفاء) links to the apodosis of the second condition. The third (لكم) is attached to (أزكى). The interpreted maṣdar (أن يؤذن لكم) is in the position of a genitive after (حتّى), attached to (تدخلوها).
Clause: «لم تجدوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the response to the vocative.
Clause: «لا تدخلوها ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
Clause: «يؤذن لكم ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «قيل لكم ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause لم تجدوا.
Clause: «ارجعوا ... » is in the position of a nominative, deputy agent of (قيل) [Note: because it is originally the quoted speech.. and according to the majority it is an explanation of the implied deputy agent, i.e. "the saying was said".].
Clause: «ارجعوا (الثانية)» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
Clause: «هو أزكى لكم» has no grammatical position, being causal.
Clause: «الله.. عليم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: or it is conjoined to the clause هو أزكى.].
Clause: «تعملون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of (ما), whether particle-like or a noun.. (بما) attached to (عليم).

* Rhetoric:
Kināya (metonymy):
In His saying, the Exalted, «حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا».
«تستأنسوا» has two aspects. One: that it is from the apparent istiʾnās (feeling at ease) which is the opposite of feeling uneasy (istīḥāsh), because one who knocks at another's door does not know whether he will be admitted or not; so he is like one uneasy from the concealment of the state from him, and when he is permitted he feels at ease. The meaning is "until you are given permission", like His saying «لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ». This is of the chapter of kināya and ridf (following), because this kind of ease follows permission, so it was put in the place of permission. The second: that it be istiʾnās in the sense of inquiry and discovery, the meaning being "until you inquire and discover the state, whether your entry is desired or not".

* Benefits:
- Occasions of revelation:
A woman of the Anṣār came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am in my house in a state in which I do not like anyone to see me, neither father nor child; then the father comes and enters upon me, and a man of my family keeps entering upon me while I am in that state." So this verse was revealed.
Abū Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, what of the inns and dwellings on the road to Syria, in which there is no inhabitant?" Then Allah revealed: ليس عليكم جناح the verse..
The houses that Allah excepted are the uninhabited ones, such as hostels, the shops of sellers, and houses built for lodging, for storing goods in them and sheltering from heat and cold, such as the houses of merchants and their shops in the markets, which people enter to sell or buy.

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(عليكم) attached to an omitted predicate of ليس, and (جناح) is the noun of ليس, nominative. (فيها) attached to the predicate of the mubtadaʾ (متاع). (لكم) attached to an omitted adjective of متاع.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تدخلوا ... ) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. "in entering".. attached to (جناح).
(ما) is a maṣdar particle in both places [Note: or a relative noun in the position of an accusative, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "what you disclose and what you conceal".]. (الواو) is conjunctive.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تبدون ... ) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object, and the maṣdar (ما تكتمون) is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to it.
Clause: «ليس عليكم جناح ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «تدخلوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «فيها متاع ... » is in the position of an accusative, a second adjective of (بيوتا) [Note: it is permissible that it be a ḥāl from (بيوتا), because it is described.].
Clause: «الله يعلم ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يعلم ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
Clause: «تبدون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما).
Clause: «تكتمون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second particle-like relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(مسكونة): feminine of مسكون, a passive participle from the triliteral verb سكن; its pattern is مفعولة.

safi-cedvel:30-31.t:
* I'rab:
(للمؤمنين) attached to (قل). (يغضّوا) a jussive imperfect, the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); the object of قل is implied, i.e. "say to them: lower your gazes". (من أبصارهم) attached to (غضّوا) [Note: (من) is redundant according to al-Akhfash; it is partitive according to al-Zamakhsharī; for explaining the genus according to Abū l-Baqāʾ - and in it there is obscurity -; and for the beginning of the limit according to Ibn ʿAṭiyya, which Abū Ḥayyān preferred.]. (الواو) is conjunctive. (لهم) attached to (أزكى). (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted and the clause after it the ṣila.].. The interpreted maṣdar (ما يصنعون) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (خبير).
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يغضّوا من أبصارهم» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition not accompanied by the fāʾ, i.e. "if you say to them 'lower', they will lower".
Clause: «يحفظوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يغضّوا.
Clause: «ذلك أزكى ... » has no grammatical position, being causal.
Clause: «إنّ الله.. خبير» has no grammatical position, being another justification.
Clause: «يصنعون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما).
31- (الواو) is conjunctive. (للمؤمنات) attached to (قل). (يغضضن) an imperfect verb indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of a jussive, the response to the request, and the (النون) is the agent pronoun. (من أبصارهنّ) attached to (يغضضن), and (هنّ) is an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يحفظن) like يغضضن and conjoined to it by the wāw; and likewise the negated verb (يبدين) is conjoined to (يحفظن or يغضضن) [Note: it is permissible that (لا) be prohibitive, in which case the verb is in the position of a jussive by it, and the clause is then conjoined to the implied clause of the quoted speech.]. (إلّا) a particle of exception. (ما) a relative noun in the position of an accusative by exception, or a substitute for زينتهنّ. (منها) attached to (ظهر). (الواو) is conjunctive. (اللام) is the lām of command. (يضربن) an imperfect verb indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of a jussive by the lām. (بخمرهنّ) attached to (يضربن), by implying in it the meaning "they let fall". (على جيوبهنّ) attached to (يضربن). (الواو) is conjunctive. (لا يبدين زينتهنّ) like the first. (إلّا) is for exception. (لبعولتهنّ) a substitute for the implied excepted, with repetition of the preposition, i.e. "let them not display their adornment to anyone of the people except to their husbands" [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the omitted excepted, i.e. "except adornment existing for their husbands".]. (أو) is a conjunction in the eleven places, and the nouns after it are conjoined to بعولتهنّ, genitive or in the position of a genitive. (ما) a relative noun with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. «ملكته». (غير) an adjective of التابعين, genitive. (من الرجال) attached to a ḥāl from التابعين - or from أولي الإربة. (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, an adjective of الطفل. (على عورات) attached to (يظهروا). (الواو) is conjunctive. (لا يضربن) like لا يبدين. (بأرجلهنّ) attached to (يضربن). (اللام) is the lām of justification. (يعلم) a passive imperfect verb, in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, deputy agent. (من زينتهنّ) attached to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun [Note: or it is a tamyīz of the relative (ما).].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلم ... ) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (يضربن).
(الواو) is resumptive. (إلى الله) attached to (توبوا). (جميعا) an accusative ḥāl from the agent of توبوا. (أيّها) an indefinite specified one addressed, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative. (المؤمنون) a substitute for أيّ, following it in being nominative in form, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
Clause: «قل (الثانية) ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause قل (the first).
Clause: «يغضضن ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition not accompanied by the fāʾ, i.e. "if you say to them 'lower your gazes', they will lower".
Clause: «يحفظن ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يغضضن.
Clause: «لا يبدين ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يغضضن or يحفظن.
Clause: «ظهر منها ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the first relative (ما).
Clause: «يضربن ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the implied quoted speech.
Clause: «لا يبدين (الثانية)» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause لا يبدين (the first) [Note: or conjoined to the clause يضربن if (لا) is prohibitive, in which case it is in the position of an accusative.].
Clause: «ملكت أيمانهنّ» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
Clause: «لم يظهروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «لا يضربن ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause يضربن..
Clause: «يعلم ما يخفين ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «يخفين ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative (ما).
Clause: «توبوا ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: it is permissible that it follow the quoted speech and be conjoined to it, and the address (to the believers) is used by way of preponderance (taghlīb).].
Clause: «أيّها المؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.
Clause: «لعلّكم تفلحون» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption - or causal. Clause: «تفلحون» is in the position of a nominative, predicate of لعلّ.

* Morphology:
(31) خمرهنّ: plural of خمار, which is a woman's head covering, a noun of a thing (ism dhāt); its pattern is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ, and the plural is فعل, with two ḍammas.
(جيوبهنّ): plural of جيب, a noun for the collar of a shirt, borrowed here for its place, namely the neck; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn, and the plural is فعول, with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and it is also said with kasra.
(الإربة): a noun for need, from أرب إلى الشيء, i.e. he needed, bāb فرح; its pattern is فعلة, with kasra then sukūn.
(عورات): plural of عورة, a noun for what must be covered from men and women; its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa then sukūn, and by analogy the plural should have fatḥa on the wāw, but it was made sukūn because vowelling a weak letter is heavy.

* Rhetoric:
1- Among the secrets that are subtle to understandings is the entry of the preposition (من) on lowering the gazes but not on the private parts, in His saying, the Exalted, «قُلْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصارِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُوا فُرُوجَهُمْ». The secret is that the matter of looking is wide. Al-Zamakhsharī said in this regard: "Do you not see that with the unmarriageable relatives (maḥārim) there is no harm in looking at their hair, chests, breasts, limbs, shins and feet, and likewise slave girls presented for sale? As for the matter of the private parts, it is narrow."
2- Fronting: in the noble verse, lowering the gazes was put before guarding the private parts, because looking is the messenger of adultery and the scout of debauchery; the trial in it is greater and more frequent, and one can hardly guard against it.
3- Exaggeration:
In His saying, the Exalted, «وَلا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا ما ظَهَرَ مِنْها» the adornment is mentioned, rather than its places, to be emphatic in the command to cover, because these adornments fall on places of the body at which it is not lawful to look except for those excepted in the verse.

* Benefits:
1- The chastity of the believer:
On the authority of ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) said: "Beware of entering upon women." A man of the Anṣār said: "What of the ḥamw?" He said: "The ḥamw is death." Related by al-Bukhārī and Muslim,
then he said: the meaning of his disapproval of entering upon women is along the lines of what is
reported from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), who said: "No man is alone with a woman but the third of them is Satan."
The ḥamw is the husband's father and whoever is related through him, such as the brother, the paternal uncle, the cousin and the like, and the wife's father and whoever is related through him. It is also said that it is only the husband's relative, and also said that it is only the wife's relative.
Abū ʿUbayd said: if this is so in the report concerning the husband's father, who is a maḥram, then what of the stranger? And the meaning of "the ḥamw is death" is that fear of him is greater than of others, evil is expected from him, and temptation is greater, because he is able to reach the woman and be alone with her without anyone objecting to him.
2- «أيها المؤمنون»:
We have seen that the one defined by «أل» is reached in calling by means of «أي», with hāʾ attached to it as a sign of the masculine, and tāʾ and hāʾ as a sign of the feminine. There are explanations on this that are consulted in their places.

safi-cedvel:32-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (منكم) attached to a ḥāl from الأيامى. (من عبادكم) attached to a ḥāl from الصالحين. (من فضله) attached to (يغنهم). (الواو) is resumptive. (عليم) a second predicate, nominative.
Clause: «أنكحوا ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يكونوا ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «يغنهم الله ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of the condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
Clause: «الله واسع ... » has no grammatical position, being a causal resumption.
33- (الواو) is conjunctive. (اللام) is the lām of command, and the sign of the jussive in (يستعفف) is the sukūn, and its end was vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns. (حتّى) a particle of limit and of genitive. (يغنيهم) an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after حتّى. (من فضله) attached to (يغنيهم).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يغنيهم ... ) is in the position of a genitive after (حتّى), attached to (يستعفف).
(الواو) is conjunctive. (الذين) a relative, mubtadaʾ, in the position of a nominative [Note: or in the position of an accusative, a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being «كاتبوا».. in which case the clause كاتبوهم has no position, being explicative.]. (ممّا) attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of يبتغون [Note: (ما) is a relative and is borrowed here for rational beings, by way of preponderance and inclusiveness.]. (الفاء) is redundant, because the mubtadaʾ resembles a condition. (علمتم) a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis. (فيهم) attached to an omitted second direct object. (الواو) is conjunctive. (من مال) attached to (آتوهم). (الذي) a relative in the position of a genitive, an adjective of مال الله, and the agent of (آتاكم) is a pronoun referring to the majestic name, and the second object is omitted, i.e. «آتاكموه». (الواو) is conjunctive. (لا) is a prohibitive, jussive lā. (على البغاء) attached to (تكرهوا). (أردن) a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of a jussive, the protasis [Note: in analyzing this condition the exegetes have many opinions.. Some made (إن) in the sense of إذ and so denied the existence of the condition altogether, so that compulsion not be interpreted as applying in the absence of their desire, though compulsion to adultery is forbidden in every case. Others made the condition depend on the desire for chastity, since there is no meaning to compulsion, nor to the condition, when they incline to adultery, for it is by their own choice... etc.]. (اللام) is for justification. (تبتغوا) an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām, and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تبتغوا ... ) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (لا تكرهوا).
(الواو) is conjunctive. (من) a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. (الفاء) is causal. (من بعد) attached to the predicate (غفور).
Clause: «يستعفف الذين ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to أنكحوا..
Clause: «لا يجدون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «يغنيهم الله ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «الذين يبتغون ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause أنكحوا..
Clause: «يبتغون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «ملكت أيمانكم ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
Clause: «كاتبوهم ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
Clause: «علمتم ... » has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.. The apodosis of the condition is omitted.. indicated by what precedes, i.e. "if you know good in them, then make a contract of manumission with them".
Clause: «آتوهم....» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause كاتبوهم. Clause: «آتاكم ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
Clause: «لا تكرهوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause أنكحوا..
Clause: «أردن ... » has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.. The apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "if they desire chastity, then do not compel them"..
Clause: «من يكرههنّ ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause لا تكرهوا..
Clause: «يكرههنّ» is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (من).
Clause: «إنّ الله.. غفور ... » has no grammatical position, being a justification for the implied apodosis, i.e.
"whoever compels them, he will be called to account, and Allah will forgive them, because Allah is forgiving" [Note: some make the stated clause itself the apodosis of the condition, with an implied link in it, i.e. "for Allah is forgiving.. to them".].

* Morphology:
(الأيامى): plural of الأيّم, a noun for one who has no spouse, whether female or male; its pattern is فيعل, taken from آم يئيم like باع يبيع, and by analogy the plural would be أيائم; the pattern of أيامى is فعالى, and it is said that there is a transposition in it, its origin being أيايم.
(الكتاب): a maṣdar meaning mukātaba, which is the contract of manumission (ʿaqd al-kitāba); its verb is كاتب, quadriliteral, and the maṣdar is samāʿī; its pattern is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ.
(البغاء): a samāʿī maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb باغت الأمة, i.e. the slave girl committed fornication; its pattern is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ, and the hamza is changed from a final yāʾ after a quiescent alif; its origin is بغاي.
(تحصّنا): a maṣdar of the quinquiliteral verb تحصّن; its pattern is تفعّل, with ḍamma on the doubled ʿayn, and the pattern of its past verb has ḍamma on the letter before the last. [Translator's note: the source as written; the past verb of تحصّن is not so vowelled in standard usage, perhaps «ما قبل آخره» refers to the maṣdar. Translated as written.]

* Rhetoric:
Iḥtirās (precaution):
In His saying, the Exalted, «إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّناً», this parenthetical was inserted to make that hideous in the mind of the one addressed and to warn him against falling into it, so that he become aware that he ought to disdain this vice even if there were no legal deterrent. The aspect of making it hideous for him is that the content of the verse is a proclamation against him that his slave girl is better than he, because she preferred chastity from indecency while he insists on compelling her.

* Benefits:
1- Urging marriage:
On the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) said: "O company of young men, whoever of you is able to marry, let him marry, for it lowers the gaze more and guards the private parts better; and whoever is not able, let him fast, for it is a protection (wijāʾ) for him." Related by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
Al-bāʾa: intercourse or marriage. What is meant is the cost of marriage.
Al-wijāʾ: crushing the testicles, and fasting is likened to castration.
2- Mukātaba: the mukātaba of a slave is that his owner says to him: "I have contracted with you for such-and-such an amount of money", so if he pays it to him, he becomes free. Its formula: the man says to his slave, "You have written for me on yourself that you will be freed by me if you fulfil to me the money, and I have written for you on myself that this will be fulfilled", or he says: "I have written upon you the fulfilment of the money, and you have written upon me the manumission." In the books of jurisprudence there are rulings of manumission to which one looks whenever a breath rises.
3- «يُغْنِهِمُ اللَّهُ»:
The verb يغني is jussive as the apodosis of the condition, and its jussive form is the dropping of the weak letter from its end.
The imperfect is also made jussive by dropping the nūn if it is one of the five verbs.
It is also made jussive by sukūn if its end is sound.
The governors of the jussive are three: a particle that makes one verb jussive, a tool that makes two verbs jussive, and the request, by making its response jussive.
